title: Unveiling of Shared Responsibility Framework for Phishing Scams
what_it_is: Unveiling of Shared Responsibility Framework for Phishing Scams

sections.label: Shared Responsibility Framework and Money Lock
sections.summary: SRF response and implementation are planned for later this year, and over 78,000 Money Lock accounts were set up, with other major retail banks to introduce it by mid-2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) when will the Shared Responsibility Framework for phishing scams be released; (b) what is the take-up rate of the Money Lock feature offered by our local banks, broken down by ages of bank customers; and (c) whether the MAS will make it mandatory for all banking institutions to participate in this initiative in the near future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We aim to publish our response to the consultation and implement the SRF later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Since the three local banks launched Money Lock in November, more than 78,000 Money Lock accounts have been set up, with over S$6.6 billion of savings set aside in March 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Among customers who have used Money Lock, those aged 50 and above make up 44%, those between 30 and 50 years old comprise 41%, and those under 30 years of age form 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Other major retail banks will introduce Money Lock by mid-2024 and the vast majority of retail depositors will have the Money Lock option available to them.

sections.label: Scams and SRF phishing focus
sections.summary: Scams can exist in a continuum of forced or unforced errors, and the SRF focuses on phishing while malware scams are also acknowledged.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It can sometimes also exist in a continuum of forced, or unforced errors based on circumstances and what public understanding is of the scams out there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We focus the SRF on phishing, but we are well aware that malware scams have also contributed to the number of scams that Singaporeans have encountered.

sections.label: Money Lock and public education
sections.summary: Not every jurisdiction's approach fits, Money Lock is encouraged to safeguard funds, and public education campaigns help against scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Not every jurisdiction's approach will fit and we need to study that carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But at the same time, to Member Desmond Choo's point, Money Lock is another feature that we are trying to encourage people to adopt to safeguard a portion of your funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We also have a very strong consolidated public education and public awareness campaign that is one of the best inoculations against scams.

sections.label: SRF rollout and scam prevention
sections.summary: Members' contributions will be factored into the SRF rollout, which is a live document, and effort will go to raising awareness and preventing scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, thank you for Members' contributions to this very important topic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We will factor all of these into consideration when we roll out SRF which is a "live" document, and also, put in a significant amount of effort to raise awareness and to prevent scams from happening.
